messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Testing measurement invariance
parts: Could you please show me if I should stop inspect the invariance across groups. If not, what should I do to test measurement invariance of this scale?

Sounds like you should read some literature on testing invariance, in particular on partial invariance (e.g., http://dx.doi.org/10.3758/s13428-013-0430-2).  You can post general questions (i.e., not software-specific) on SEMNET, which is a much larger forum of SEM experts.  Once you know what method you need to use, you might find the partialInvariance() function in the semTools package useful.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

I conduct weak invariance testing manually as following:
>conf<-'Anger=~NA*Agg_2+Agg_7
PhVe=~NA*Agg_1+Agg_3+Agg_4+Agg_5+Agg_6+Agg_8+Agg_9+Agg_10+Agg_11
Anger~~c(1,1)*Anger
PhVe~~c(1,1)*PhVe'
>weak <- 'Anger =~ NA*Agg_2+Agg_7
PhVe =~ NA*Agg_1+Agg_3+Agg_4+Agg_5+Agg_6+Agg_8+Agg_9+Agg_10+Agg_11
Anger ~~ c(1, NA)*Anger
PhVe ~~ c(1, NA)*PhVe'
But when I run configural <- cfa(conf, data = completeAgr, group="School") it had a warning: Error in lavaanify(model = FLAT, meanstructure = lavoptions$meanstructure,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier () of element Anger~~Anger.
Does anyone know how to solve this problem?
Thanks you very much,
Tuan.
